titulo: Does searing a steak seal in the juices?
fuentes: America's Test Kitchen / Cook's Illustrated, 'Searing steak' test: https://www.americastestkitchen.com/how_tos/5699-searing-steak (8 rib-eyes; seared first vs. last; both batches lost about 22% of their weight in liquid)

frases.texto: You sear your steak to seal in the juices.
frases.estilo: Dry and confident, like catching a grill master in the act.
Short and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: A seared crust doesn't seal anything. Steaks lose juice as they cook, seared or not.
That sizzle you love? It's mostly water on the surface of the meat turning to steam in the hot pan.
America's Test Kitchen tested it with rib-eyes, and steaks lost about the same amount of juice whether they were seared first or last.
So why sear? Because browning adds flavor and a crust.
Heads up: searing is still worth it. It just isn't a seal.
Tonight, sear for the crust and the flavor, not for the juice.
Send this to the friend who swears the sear locks it all in.
frases.estilo: Playful, with humor, as a punchline.
